compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Part of bug 6798 (the advisory `sweep (windows)` job is red at a scale that hides new regressions). The user chose, on 2026-10-26, to narrow that job to a maintained subset and hold the subset green. This task is the first narrowing step.

Scheduled run 40284466555 (ref 6080140e7af, 2026-10-26) ended `1652 failed, 18031 passed, 134 skipped, 39 errors`. Of the 1679 distinct failing node ids, 470 are under `tests/scripts/` (53 modules). Most of those modules drive the Linux host-operations scripts under `infra/scripts/` (observability, autodeploy, docker/journald/var-tmp caps, container caps, user-data device resolution) through `bash` against PATH stubs of `systemctl`, `journalctl`, `docker`, `df` and similar. Those scripts only ever run on the Linux deploy host, so a Windows result for them carries no information about rebar's Windows behaviour; Linux CI already runs them in the gating cell.

## Approach
In `tests/conftest.py`, extend `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (next to the existing path-based `platform_compat` marking) so that on `sys.platform == "win32"` every test whose repo-relative path matches a named set of Linux-host-script fragments gets a `pytest.mark.skip` with a reason that names this ticket. The matching and the platform decision live in one small pure helper, `_linux_host_script_skip_reason(relative_posix, platform)`, which returns the reason string or `None`, so the rule is unit-testable without Windows and `pytest_collection_modifyitems` gains one call and no new branch beyond it. Fragments (path prefixes, so future tests for the same scripts are covered): `tests/scripts/test_observability_`, `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_`, `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap`, `tests/scripts/test_container_cap`, `tests/scripts/test_journald_cap`, `tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap`, `tests/unit/test_user_data_device_resolution`. Nothing is skipped on Linux or macOS. No new marker, fixture, environment variable, config key or CI step is added.

Known cost: whole modules are skipped on Windows, including a few tests that currently pass there (measured in the evidence comment). They check Linux-script behaviour that Linux CI already gates, so the loss is no Windows signal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_linux_host_script_skip_reason` returns a reason naming this ticket for each of the 7 fragments when the platform is `win32`, and `None` for those same paths on `linux` and `darwin` and for an unrelated path on `win32`. Checked by a new unit test, `tests/unit/test_conftest_windows_skip_rule.py`, which fails before the helper exists and passes after.
- [ ] On Linux, `pytest --collect-only -q` over the 7 fragment paths collects the same node ids before and after the change, and none are skipped. Checked by diffing the two collect listings.
- [ ] With `sys.platform` patched to `win32` in a subprocess collection, every node under the 7 fragments carries a skip whose reason names this ticket, and every node whose skip reason names this ticket is under one of the 7 fragments. Checked by a collection run whose output is recorded in the evidence comment; skips from other causes are not counted.
- [ ] `make verify` ends with only the known 17 arm64 pandoc failures under `tests/unit/reconciler`, and the Gerrit change reaches `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.

## Out of scope
The other failure classes of 6798: the offline network guard (about 400), `Filename too long` (about 177), the encoding tail, and the two large `tests/unit` modules `test_review_bot.py` and `test_gate_step_tree_skew.py`. Each gets its own task under 6798.
